title: Scoped fan-out code review — disjoint accountability over a shared full-diff context
summary: Prior-art survey for #3326 (scoped fan-out review), prepared 2026-08-27. THE FRAMING FINDING — two interventions get called "decomposing a review" and only one has a controlled positive result: splitting the ACCOUNTABILITY while every reviewer reads the whole artifact (Porter/Votta/Basili, IEEE TSE 1995, 16 three-person teams) raised detection ~35% at p<.01, while splitting the INPUT into separately-reviewed pieces (di Biase et al., PeerJ CS 2019, 28 developers) reduced wrongly-reported issues and had NO effect on defects found. Porter also ruled out the resampling placebo — each scenario group was best at its own fault class and no better than other scenario reviewers off it, so the lens CONTENT carried the gain — and one of its three original scenarios was literally "Missing or Ambiguous Functionalities", i.e. an omission seat. FINDING 2 — no production ownership system records who approved which file: GitHub CODEOWNERS (last-match-wins routing, no path on the review object), Google Critique (private non-gating checkbox), Gerrit code-owners (per-file STATUS derived, but "It is not possible to approve individual files only", justified by owned-set staleness), Phabricator Owners (package-granular reviewer rows) and Chromium all partition the REQUIREMENT by path and keep the APPROVAL whole-change; Google and Chromium independently converged on stating the partition in a comment. FINDING 3 — the untangling line (ClusterChanges' def-use projection over 1000 Office changesets, ~42% with >1 non-trivial partition; SmartCommit 71-84%; Flexeme 0.81; UTango +9.9%) measures decomposition ACCURACY against a ground-truth partition and never review effectiveness. FINDING 4 — the ~200-400 LOC ceiling is a vendor book: defect counts hand-coded from a 300-review sample, "defect" includes style preferences, the 400 is DERIVED from a 60-minute attention claim, declining density rests on a self-disclosed constant-true-density assumption, and no peer-reviewed replication exists (Microsoft's measured onset is 20+ FILES; Kononenko finds a continuous effect with no inflection). Coverity's "churn cap" is a <=5%-per-release stability budget on how much the reported defect set may SHIFT BETWEEN TOOL VERSIONS — not a cap on code analysed — and it is what forbids randomization. FINDING 5 — shipped AI reviewers chunk as a context workaround (PR-Agent compresses and skips whole files, /review is single-shot; CodeRabbit's per-file concurrency is documented as rate-limit throughput; AutoCommenter is one file at a time with NO cross-file reasoning; Cursor BugBot V1 ran eight order-randomized passes with majority voting and was DELETED). Exactly one publishes disjoint accountability with a COVERAGE RECEIPT — Qwen Code /review: "a chunk with no receipt is re-reviewed before the run proceeds", plus the warning that territory alone silently fails ("What they lacked was not the lines but the question"). FINDING 6 — Sovrano/Bauer/Bacchelli measured the LLM-specific mechanism: models are "lost in the end" of long inputs and naive chunking bought >37% average recall across models and CWE types, AT A PRECISION COST. FINDING 7 — do not vote and do not debate: majority voting beats every multi-agent-debate configuration at matched compute, conformity averages 47.2% with 57-77% of flips correct->wrong and the STRONGER agent caving, while the minority holds the correct answer in ~1 of 4 disagreements because shared pretraining correlates errors. FINDING 8 (the reduction trap) — Ribeiro et al.: three analyzers at 0.57/0.16/0.08 precision union to 0.39, i.e. toward the pool MEAN; a learned filter lifted it to 0.68 retaining 95.8% of real flaws. Union-then-rank-then-filter, never union-and-report. WHAT THE REPO'S OWN DATA ADDS — median merged PR is 4 files/317 lines so the dial is inert on ~75% of PRs; directory-prefix sharding degenerates (10 of the 15 largest put >=47% of files under one prefix, one is 100% a flat directory); churn-balancing takes the largest shard from 79% to 17% but 44% of that PR's churn is generated fixtures, so weight must be risk-adjusted; and two runs of the SAME reviewer on the SAME commit share ZERO findings (micro-churn 1.0, n=5 pairs), which means resampling may explain any gain from N seats. That is why #3326 ships maxShards at 1 and carries a scoped-vs-unscoped A/B, reporting recall AND precision per arm, as its one falsifiable criterion. Full grounding in we:reports/2026-08-27-scoped-fan-out-code-review.md.
